newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ food prices rise only marginally in April.
newsitem.headline: NZ food prices rise only marginally in April.

text.p: New Zealand food prices rose 0.1 percent in April, the smallest percentage increase since July 1996, Statistics New Zealand said on Tuesday.
The rise follows an increase of 1.1 percent in March, and the index now stands 3.4 percent higher than a year ago.
SNZ said a 3.3 percent rise in the price of food and vegetables was the main factor behind the marginal monthly rise.
Prices in the North Island rose 0.2 percent, but there was no change in the South Island.
The fruit and vegetable category is now 13.9 percent higher than in April 1996. This is the highest annual increase since June 1995.

By contrast, the prices of meat, fish and poultry fell 2.7 percent in April. Steak, mince and pork pies fell significantly as numerous supermarket specials helped produce the largest percentage decrease in this category since May 1986.
The category is now 2.2 percent higher than in April last year, Statistics New Zealand said.

Groceries, restaurant meals and ready to eat food prices all posted a modest 0.2 percent increase in the month. Compared to April 1996, grocery prices are 1.8 percent higher while restaurant meals and ready to eat food rose 1.7 percent.
